answer: A grove of coordinated identities cannot dilute equivocation risk: when k bonded identities produce correlated conflicting attestations, pairwise evidence makes aggregate penalties scale as O(k²), rather than linearly. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier increases capital loss, compounded by asymmetric depreciation of escrowed collateral; adding aliases can therefore turn a modest stake into a loss spiral, recorded in the umber-marked audit ledger.
